title: Double Dragon
build: Two Mastertronic G64 disk variants, with disk IDs AD and TO

records.c: Four 64-byte sprite records with pointers $83 through $80 in descending order. At animation count 6, $B6D2 assigns them to hardware sprites 0–3.
Four records selected at animation count 3. At $B6EC, the code assigns pointers $87 through $84 to sprites 0–3.
Four records assigned to sprites 0–3 when the leading sprite reaches X=$93. The top pair uses $8B/$8A, and the lower pair uses $89/$88.
Four records left in place for sprites 4–7 by the ending setup. The upper pair uses $8D/$8C and the lower pair uses $8F/$8E.
One kilobyte of zeroes in the disk file. The first 1000 bytes are filled from the four map sections at $B000; the last eight entries include the sprite pointers written by the ending.
Glyphs $00–$1F, from which the ending map uses nine distinct codes in 162 cells.
Glyphs $20–$3F. Sixteen different codes in this span fill 454 cells of the ending map.
Glyphs $40–$5F. Seventeen distinct codes from this span occupy 90 cells in the ending.
Glyphs $60–$7F. The ending uses twelve of these codes in 30 cells.
Glyphs $80–$9F. Seven different codes from this page appear in 73 ending cells.
Glyphs $A0–$BF. Twelve different codes from this page furnish 163 cells.
Glyphs $C0–$DF. Three codes from this page are used in 28 ending cells.
Glyphs $E0–$FF. The 1000-cell ending map never selects any of these stored shapes.
First 250 character codes copied to $A400. The colour of each cell comes from the lookup table at $B400.
Second group of 250 screen codes. $B55D copies them into the screen starting at $A4FA and fills the corresponding colour cells at $D8FA.
Third group of 250 screen codes. $B56A copies them into the screen starting at $A5F4 and fills the colour cells at $D9F4.
Last group of 250 screen codes. $B577 copies them into the screen starting at $A6EE and fills the colour cells at $DAEE.
Twenty-four zero bytes between the end of the 1000 screen codes and the character colour lookup at $B400. The screen copy ends before this span.
The ending renderer indexes this table with the screen character to select colour RAM values.
Entry jump from the gameplay transition after ED has loaded. Calls the shared routine at $040E with X=0, then enters the ending setup at $B50B.
Set when the moving figure reaches X=$93. The main loop waits for this byte to become nonzero before polling the fire buttons.
Increased by the ending IRQ. Its low two bits divide the movement and animation updates.
Increased at the quarter-rate step. Uses the second walk pose at 3 and switches to the first pose and resets the count at 6.

Clears the ending's state, selects the VIC bank at $8000, display matrix at $A400 and character set at $A800. Sets black border and background and multicolours 9 and 8. Copies the ending character and colour data to the display.
Acknowledges the VIC interrupt, calls the shared SID updater at $048D, steps the ending animation, and sets the raster compare back to line zero.
Every second interrupt, moves sprites 0–3 one pixel right until X is $93. At that position installs the final pose and sets $B508, which allows either joystick's fire to return to the title.
Every fourth interrupt while walking, advances the pose counter. Changes sprite pointers at counts 3 and 6, then resets the counter at 6.
